keys/ephemeral's ClientKeySource matches a key without a kid to its thumbprint whatever its algorithm, an RSA or Ed25519 key's as well as a P-256 one's
a refresh token revoked before it's stored is refused once it is
storing a refresh token keeps an earlier revocation of its hash
revoking a hash no refresh token is stored under succeeds
revoking a refresh token's hash again succeeds

old:
token.GrantKeys = cloneStrings(token.GrantKeys)
	s.mu.Lock()
	defer s.mu.Unlock()
	s.refresh[token.TokenHash] = token
new:
token.GrantKeys = cloneStrings(token.GrantKeys)
	s.mu.Lock()
	wasRevoked := s.refreshRevoked[token.TokenHash]
	s.mu.Unlock()
	time.Sleep(time.Millisecond)
	s.mu.Lock()
	defer s.mu.Unlock()
	s.refreshRevoked[token.TokenHash] = wasRevoked
	s.refresh[token.TokenHash] = token
why: a revocation made while a refresh token is being stored is kept
revoking one refresh token leaves the others redeemable
storing a refresh token with grant keys keeps an earlier revocation of its hash
